title: Nebula Finance - Private VPC discovery
summary: Initial discovery on private VPC deployment for Nebula Finance. Confirmed security requirements (SOC2, KMS), network topology constraints (no public egress from prod VPC, cross-account peering preferred, limited regions us-east-1 and eu-west-1), and desire to evaluate Redwood Private with VPC peering or Private Endpoint. Next steps: share security pack, network diagram, schedule technical deep dive and benchmark run in staging.
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 + network/security docs (Daniel)
Customer to share current VPC diagram and allowed CIDR ranges (Aisha)
Schedule deep-dive w/ infra team and SE to walk peering options (Riya/Daniel)
Set up trial cluster + run lightweight latency/cost benchmark (Riya)
action_items: Daniel Kim: Send SOC2 + security pack by 2027-01-14
Aisha Rahman: Share VPC diagram and CIDR blocks by 2027-01-15
Riya Patel: Schedule technical deep-dive and send calendar invite by 2027-01-13
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-01-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Daniel Kim (Redwood AE), Riya Patel (Redwood SE), Michael Torres (CTO - Nebula), Aisha Rahman (Network Eng), Leah Chen (Security), Rajiv Nair (Infra)

Summary: Initial discovery focused on Private/VPC deployment. Discussed peering models, private endpoints, regional constraints, compliance and next steps.

[00:00] Daniel (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick intros, i'm daniel kim, AE at Redwood, with riya our systems engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Michael (Nebula): hey, good thanks. michael here, cto. we wanna figure out how we can run models in our VPCs, minimal public egress, tight audit.
[00:15] Aisha (Network): hey. aisha - network. main constraints: cross-account peering only, no internet-routable endpoints from prod, and limited regions we operate in - us-east-1 primary, eu-west-1 secondary.
[00:23] Riya (Redwood SE): thanks. thats helpful. a couple ways we usually run for private deployments: either VPC peering / cross-account peering from your VPC to the Redwood Private infra, or a Private Endpoint (interface endpoint) that we surface into your network. each has tradeoffs.
[00:36] Leah (Security): quick Q - does redwood boot in our account or in redwood-managed account? we need kms control, audit logs forwarded to our splunk.
[00:43] Daniel: good question. we support both patterns. for most enterprise customers we offer a customer-managed deployment where the control plane can be private and data plane runs in your VPC (or we run in a redwood-managed account with strict tenancy and dedicated nodes). you can bring your own KMS in the customer-managed model.
[00:56] Rajiv (Infra): if we're doing cross-account peering, how do you handle routing and security groups \u2014 do we need a transit gateway?
[01:03] Riya: you can use VPC peering for a single account pair, or TGW for many VPCs. for high scale across many accounts a TGW is recommended; peering works if it's just one or two. note that peering is regional - for cross-region we either do inter-region peering or an endpoint in each region.
[01:20] Michael: our compliance folks will want no public IP on the inference nodes. is that possible?
[01:25] Daniel: yes, with private endpoints or by placing nodes in your private subnets behind NAT rules that block outbound internet. we also support egress via customer-managed NAT with strict egress rules so telemetry goes to approved endpoints only.
[01:37] Aisha: about DNS - if you provide an interface endpoint, do we need to change resolvers? we prefer not to touch global resolvers if possible.
[01:44] Riya: typically an interface endpoint creates private dns entries that map the service name to internal ENIs. you can opt in to the private dns, or manage a split-horizon. either way we can provide a playbook.
[01:55] Michael: are there region restrictions on the model variants or quantized runtimes? we run models in us-east-1 primarily, but some data residency in eu-west-1.
[02:03] Riya: models are available where we've deployed the runtime. for Redwood Private we can deploy to eu-west-1 and us-east-1; if you need specialized hardware we may have suggestions (e.g., A100 vs H100). there can be slight performance differences and kernel selection per region but we handle that in the runtime.
[02:18] Leah: security - SOC 2 reports, iso, how does redwood handle log retention and audit access?
[02:24] Daniel: we'll share SOC 2 and a security pack. audit logs can be forwarded to your logging endpoint via syslog or S3; for customer-managed deployment you can keep logs in your S3 and bring KMS keys.
[02:35] Rajiv: on networking ports, which ports need to be open? and what about egress to update images/kernels?
[02:41] Riya: primary control plane communication is HTTPS (443). we need pod-to-control-plane and management plane comms - we'll provide exact CIDRs. for image pulls, if you want no public egress, we can mirror images to your private registry or use S3 with VPC endpoints.
[02:55] Aisha: any experience with cross-account peering policy -> we have strict security group rules, namespace scoping.
[03:01] Riya: yep, we typically recommend least privilege security groups and explicit ACLs. for TGW you can centralize routing. we also have guidance for IAM roles tied to the node instances so there is no shared credential.
[03:14] Michael: pricing question - difference between Dedicated reserved capacity and Private in-vpc?
[03:20] Daniel: Dedicated is more about reserved GPU pools (redwood-managed) with predictable throughput and SLA. Private/VPC is a deployment model; pricing depends on whether you host in your account (you pay infra) vs redwood-hosted dedicated nodes. we can send a pricing matrix.
[03:33] Michael: ok. we need cost estimates to compare to our in-house gpu farm.
[03:37] Daniel: understood. we'll send pricing plus a sample cost-per-token and unit economics for your workload.
[03:42] Leah: what's the onboarding timeline? our procurement cycle is 6-8 weeks typically.
[03:47] Daniel: for a pilot, we can get a sandbox up in 2-4 weeks depending on approvals and network changes. production posture with audit signoffs usually spans 6-12 weeks.
[03:58] Rajiv: any firewall appliances or hardware we should plan for?
[04:01] Riya: usually not. if you run perimeter appliances they'll sit in the path for egress; internally we just need routing and security groups. for high-throughput we can recommend placement and MTU tuning.
[04:12] Michael: crosstalk \u2014 sorry \u2014 do you support private endpoints across accounts without peering (like AWS PrivateLink)?
[04:18] Riya: yes, PrivateLink / interface endpoints work cross-account and avoid peering; downside is you might need an endpoint per AZ and per region for HA. peering is simpler for direct connectivity but doesn't support transitive routing.
[04:31] Aisha: performance wise, is PrivateLink latency worse? we are latency sensitive on live inference.
[04:36] Riya: usually a small delta; peering/TGW tends to be slightly lower latency. we can run a benchmark in your environment to measure tail latency.
[04:46] Michael: can you run an eval of our prompt set? we want quality checks and regression monitoring.
[04:51] Daniel: yes, Redwood Optimize and our rollout tooling will let you tie regression alerts to prompt sets. we'll include an eval template.
[04:58] Leah: KMS - do we get to control key rotation and access?
[05:02] Daniel: for customer-managed deployments yes. you'll retain key ownership. for redwood-managed we use dedicated keys and can give audit access; both models available.
[05:12] Rajiv: what about data residency \u2014 if a model has to run in eu-west-1, can you guarantee keys and compute never leave region?
[05:19] Riya: yes, we can deploy in-region and keep logs and keys in-region if needed. we'll document the architecture for an in-region-only flow.
[05:28] Michael: great. next steps?
[05:30] Daniel: we'll send security docs (SOC2, pen test summary), a network playbook with required CIDRs and ports, and a pricing + pilot plan. riya will schedule the technical deep dive.
[05:41] Riya: i'll reach out to set up the deep-dive and request a staging VPC so we can run latency and throughput bench.
[05:47] Aisha: i'll share our VPC diagrams and CIDRs. note we need all endpoints approved by our security review.
[05:53] Leah: please include specifics on log forwarding and KMS in the packet.
[05:58] Daniel: noted. unless theres anything else we'll wrap. thanks everyone.
[06:03] Michael: thanks, good session.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "K-V cash" instead of KV cache), product references sometimes truncated ("Redwood Dedicate" etc.).
